header.running_head: The Bravery of Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddeeq (RA)

blocks.text: who would remain with Rasulullaah ﷺ so that the Mushrikeen do not attack him. (Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) volunteered for the task when all others were unable to.) By Allaah! Whenever a Mushrik even drew close to us Abu Bakr (RA) was there with his sword drawn near the head side of Rasulullaah ﷺ. He attacked anyone who dared attack Rasulullaah ﷺ. He was certainly the bravest of people." [^1]
The Bravery of Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA)

Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) says, "I know of no person who did not make Hijrah secretly except for Umar bin Khattaab (RA). When he decided to make Hijrah, he hung his sword from his neck, carried his bow on his shoulder and took a few arrows in his hand. He then proceeded to the Kabah where the leaders of the Quraysh were sitting in their gatherings. He went around the Kabah seven times and then performed two Rakaahs salaah by the Maqaam Ibraheem. Thereafter, he approached each gathering separately, saying, "May your faces be disfigured! Whoever wants his mother to mourn him, his children to become orphans and his wife to become a widow should meet me behind this valley (to try and stop my Hijrah)." None dared follow him out. [^2]
The Bravery of Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA)
The Poem of Hadhrat Ali (RA) after the Battle of Uhud
Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that after the Battle of Uhud, Hadhrat Ali (RA) came home to Hadhrat Faatima (RA) and said the following couplets (which meant):

"O Faatima! Take this flawless sword from me
I am neither shaken (with fear) nor a worthless man
By my life! I have truly exerted myself to assist Muhammad ﷺ
and for the pleasure of my Rabb Who has complete knowledge about His bondsmen"

Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "If you think that you fought well, so have Sahal bin Hunayf and Ibn Simma." Rasulullaah ﷺ also mentioned the name of a third Sahabi (RA) whose name a narrator called Mu'alla had forgotten. Hadhrat Jibra'eel (AS) commented, "O Muhammad ﷺ! I swear by your father that this is certainly an occasion of grief." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Jibra'eel! He (Hadhrat Ali (RA)) is from me." To this, Hadhrat Jibra'eel (AS) said, "And I am from the two of you (with you two always)." [^3]
